top_story: The US disabling of a commercial ship attempting to leave Iran marks a sharp escalation around the blockade and increases the risk that Tehran will act on its pledge to challenge interdiction in and around the Strait of Hormuz. The pattern across both arenas is coercion aimed beyond immediate military targets, with civilians absorbing long-term biological, economic, and psychological damage. The regional picture is one of widening confrontation in which pressure tactics are hardening and the human consequences are becoming more structural and irreversible.
